claims.statement: The exact generator reproduces polynomials through each declared candidate and optimal-stencil degree for orders 5--15, with positive optimal weights summing exactly to one.
Generated order five reproduces the known Jiang--Shu coefficients and agrees with the independently written GradFlow WENO-5 scalar seed within its frozen oracle bound.

The qualified scalar periodic implementation converges on the smooth family and remains conservative, differentiable, device-consistent, and full-graph compilable for the tested orders and representative gates.
Classical WENO-JS loses design order on the frozen higher-order critical-point family; the loss is formulation behavior, not hidden by retuning epsilon.
The generated reconstruction transfers through the qualified face-frozen Roe-characteristic 3-D Euler path for orders 5--15 under its distinct Shu epsilon, LF, grid, and time-integration contract.

A scalar binary32 indicator/weight-formation seam can preserve frozen accuracy and accelerate compiled execution, but the same policy does not satisfy the strict higher-order characteristic-Euler contract.
Logical single-owner face reconstruction reduces ordinary-PyTorch 3-D RHS time at every valid screened endpoint and reduces compiler temporary allocation at moderate/large sizes.
The matched native-CUDA WENO-5 face-once schedule exhibits an approximately twofold large-grid resident speedup but pays approximately twofold global workspace.
Coefficient-basis diagnostics and exact rational complexity grow strongly with order, while sampled roundoff onset moves to progressively coarser grids under the A1 scalar contract.

Scalar epsilon 1e-29 is numerically indistinguishable from the 1e-40 comparison lane in the frozen N=128 amplitude range; larger epsilons can materially change scale-dependent smooth and critical cases.

Earlier sampled roundoff onset at higher order is consistent with growing coefficient/expression sensitivity, but A1 does not causally apportion the floor among coefficient conversion, evaluation order, cancellation, and input rounding.
The complete matched order-5--15 cold/warm/AOT/CPU/GPU performance surface is not yet measured.
No independently gradient-checked inverse or sensitivity application has yet demonstrated differentiable utility.
MPS, orders above 15, general boundaries in multiple dimensions, Navier--Stokes, curvilinear geometry, and production aerospace workflows remain unqualified.
GradFlow is the first arbitrary-order WENO generator, first PyTorch WENO, first differentiable WENO, or first GPU WENO.
Finite-difference WENO, PyTorch, GPUs, or GradFlow are universally faster or superior across formulations and endpoints.
Current GradFlow is a general, real-time, production-ready aerospace CFD solver.

prior_art.title: OpenSBLI automatic finite-difference CFD code generation
prior_art.spatial_formulation: explicit high-order finite difference on structured curvilinear multi-block grids
prior_art.weno_family_orders: WENO-JS arbitrary odd order; WENO-Z global indicators implemented through order 13 in inspected source; TENO also available
prior_art.coefficient_policy: SymPy Rational generation of ENO coefficients and optimal weights plus dynamic polynomial/integral generation of Jiang-Shu smoothness indicators
prior_art.reconstruction: characteristic Lax-Friedrichs WENO; component and shock-filter paths also present
prior_art.implementation: high-level Python/Einstein notation to OPS C/C++ source transformation
prior_art.hardware: OpenMP, MPI, CUDA, OpenCL, OpenACC, and multi-GPU through OPS
prior_art.correctness_performance: validation/verification suite, shock-boundary-layer DNS, and multi-architecture scaling; exact GradFlow-matched timing not available
prior_art.maintenance_license: maintained; inspected official commit dated 2026-08-05; GPLv3

prior_art.title: PyWENO
prior_art.spatial_formulation: one-dimensional WENO reconstruction toolkit, primarily cell-average reconstruction; not a complete FD PDE solver
prior_art.weno_family_orders: arbitrarily high order and arbitrary reconstruction points
prior_art.coefficient_policy: symbolically generates smoothness coefficients, reconstruction coefficients, and optimal weights
prior_art.reconstruction: scalar kernels; downstream PyClaw can reconstruct characteristic fields
prior_art.implementation: Python/SymPy generator; generated C, C++, OpenCL, CUDA, and Fortran building blocks
prior_art.hardware: depends on generated target and host solver
prior_art.correctness_performance: tests and PyClaw use; no current GradFlow-matched benchmark
prior_art.maintenance_license: last inspected commit 2021-03-08, outside the 24-month maintained window; BSD-style license

prior_art.title: PyClaw: Accessible, Extensible, Scalable Tools for Wave Propagation Problems
prior_art.spatial_formulation: finite-volume/wave-propagation reconstruction, not Jiang-Shu finite-difference flux reconstruction
prior_art.coefficient_policy: symbolically generated by PyWENO, then emitted as standalone Fortran kernels
prior_art.reconstruction: componentwise or characteristic reconstruction through host Riemann solvers
prior_art.implementation: Python interface with automatically wrapped Fortran kernels and PETSc parallelism
prior_art.hardware: large CPU systems in the paper; generated low-level kernels
prior_art.correctness_performance: paper reports applications and scalable performance, not a matched GradFlow endpoint
prior_art.maintenance_license: archival paper; current Clawpack maintenance was not used to classify the historical PyWENO path

prior_art.title: HOPE: an arbitrary-order non-oscillatory finite-volume shallow water dynamical core with automatic differentiation
prior_art.spatial_formulation: genuinely two-dimensional finite-volume shallow-water reconstruction on a cubed sphere
prior_art.coefficient_policy: generated high-order polynomial reconstruction; not the Jiang-Shu FD flux construction
prior_art.reconstruction: two-dimensional WENO with adaptive polynomial-order reduction
prior_art.implementation: PyTorch using convolution and Einstein summation; companion Fortran convergence implementation
prior_art.correctness_performance: standard shallow-water tests, conservation, up to 11th-order accuracy, and about 2x RTX 3090 versus dual Xeon E5-2699v4 reported
prior_art.maintenance_license: 2025 archival paper and Zenodo code; redistribution governed by cited deposits

prior_art.title: JAX-Fluids / JAX-Fluids 2.0
prior_art.spatial_formulation: primarily finite-volume Godunov CFD, with a separate conservative characteristic/component flux-splitting path that materially overlaps FD-WENO algebra
prior_art.weno_family_orders: hard-coded WENO 1, 3, 5, 6, 7, and 9 plus variants; no 11, 13, or 15 registration found in inspected source
prior_art.coefficient_policy: explicit per-order constants and expressions; WENO9-JS is visibly hard-coded
prior_art.reconstruction: primitive, conservative, component flux splitting, and characteristic flux splitting
prior_art.hardware: CPU, GPU, TPU; JAX-Fluids 2.0 reports scaling to hundreds of accelerators
prior_art.correctness_performance: published verification, complex 3-D cases, stable long-horizon gradients, and HPC scaling; no identical GradFlow formulation comparison
prior_art.maintenance_license: maintained; inspected official commit dated 2026-08-26; GPLv3

prior_art.title: JAX-Shock: A Differentiable, GPU-Accelerated, Shock-Capturing Neural Solver for Compressible Flow Simulation
prior_art.spatial_formulation: compressible Navier-Stokes shock-capturing; finite-difference versus finite-volume classification not established from accessible evidence
prior_art.reconstruction: system solver; exact characteristic policy unknown
prior_art.correctness_performance: preprint reports direct simulation, sequence learning, and reverse-mode physical-parameter inference
prior_art.maintenance_license: 2026 preprint; official source repository and license were not located
